incident-bot: PagerDuty: page fired -> INC-3255556789 for service=canary-heartbeat (severity: info). Metric 'heartbeat.missed' crossed threshold in us-west-2. Link: <https://pagerduty.com/incidents/INC3255556789|INC-3255556789>
Maya: acked and taking. I'm on it.
incident-bot: Ack received from Maya.
Jay: oncall here — looking at the canary dashboard now. Pulling metrics.
Maya: quick snapshot: 23:01:15 UTC a ~20s spike in missed heartbeats, immediate recovery by 23:01:40. No corresponding 5xx spike in prod-app.
Rafa: any customer reports?
Maya: none. SLOs appear unchanged (p50/p95 stable). Looks like a synthetic canary blip.
Jay: grabbing canary-runner logs now.
Maya: logs show a transient timeout then retry success.
Jay: 
```bash
2026-03-15T23:01:15Z canary-runner[42]: request timeout (10s)
2026-03-15T23:01:16Z canary-runner[42]: retry -> success
```
Maya: incident-bot auto-resolved the PD page at 23:02:04 UTC :white_check_mark:
Rafa: mm ok auto-resolve. Is this a one-off? I see 2 similar flaps earlier in the last 6h.
Jay: confirmed 3 brief spikes total, all coincide with a scheduled CI/infra job burst window. Suggests noisy signal from transient worker saturation.
Maya: mitigation: I'll mute the canary-heartbeat alert for 10m to avoid thrash and open a follow-up to tune thresholds.
Maya: /remind @sre-lead to review canary thresholds tomorrow.
ops-bot: Created ticket INF-8423: "tune canary heartbeat threshold and backoff" -> https://tracker/redwood/INF-8423
Rafa: +1. Also propose improving runner backoff logic (fewer false positives).
Jay: proposal for alert tuning (suggested):
```yaml
alert:
  name: canary-heartbeat
  trigger: misses >= 3
  window: 60s
```
Jay: this would require 3 misses in 60s instead of 1 miss in 15s — reduces sensitivity to short bursts.
Maya: sounds good. I'll own the change and coordinate rollout. No customer impact observed, marking as no-impact brief.
Jay: can we also throttle the runner concurrency during CI windows? I'll check scheduler.
Maya: I'll keep the thread open for 1hr and close if no repeats.
incident-bot: Thread auto-closed by Maya at 23:05:34 UTC.
Maya: thanks :raised_hands:
Jay: thanks — following up on scheduler side.
Rafa: if this repeats we'll move to postmortem bucket. For now file INF-8423 covers next steps.
